A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RUE research. Their complete main text, equations, figures and appendices are readable and matchable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G report original bandit simulations, including error probabilities, two-stage parameter sensitivity and performance across arm counts.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A.7 retain original simulations and report additional TTTS results in the arm-count comparison.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the estimation equations retain the same RUE procedure: initialize with two pulls per arm, compute random-effect estimates, select using 2 log n exploration and recommend the largest estimated mean. The theoretical corrections do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same random-mean setups R1–R3 and fixed-mean Bernoulli setups F1–F6. The non-Gaussian-prior discussion concerns existing experiments. Hyperparameter optimization is proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: TTTS joins SR, SH and UCBE in the appendix arm-count comparison, Figure S.2 in v1 versus Figure 4 in v2. TTTS was already plotted in v1 Figures 1 and 2, so its addition to the main-text baseline description does not establish a new comparator there.

E3.justification: Reward distributions, arm counts, budget grids and error-probability evaluation remain unchanged. The added TTTS scaling results use the existing settings. Figure 2's corrected scenario headings do not represent changes to the experimental arm counts.

E4.justification: The existing analysis of performance as arm count increases gains TTTS comparisons at K = 40 and 80, modestly extending its comparative evidence. The two-stage q sensitivity analysis and existing tests outside the Gaussian-prior assumptions are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 sampled instances with standard-error bars and boxplots in Figure 1. The appendix retains 1000 independent executions and the same uncertainty-reporting conventions, including standard errors below 0.016 for the scaling comparison. No new seed or significance reporting appears.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds TTTS error-probability results for F4 at K = 40 and 80, showing lower errors for RUE. Its K = 20 TTTS results were already present in v1 Figure 2. Main-figure results and the existing SR, SH, UCBE and RUE scaling curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 changes the gap-probability definition from a supremum of individual probabilities to the probability of a small best-versus-second-best gap, aligning it with the existing appendix proof. V2 adds factors of two to tail terms in Theorems 5.1–5.2 and Appendix A.3. Section 5.1 changes the sufficient condition on delta from equality to an inequality and corrects the approximation for m from a denominator of 5 to 25. These are localized revisions; the principal rates and proof structure remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and central conclusion retain the same Bayesian BAI formulation, RUE method, instance-independent bounds of order square root of K/n up to logarithmic factors, and broad empirical advantages. The new application suggestion does not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds an explanation of the inflated Gaussian-likelihood variance required by the bound. Section 6 explicitly acknowledges mixed performance against TTTS in R3 and TTTS advantages at the largest budget in F4 and F6, already visible in v1's plots. The conclusion adds hyperparameter optimization as a potential application; existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly states explicitly that RUE requires no hyperparameters because it uses estimated variances. This is a limited implementation clarification: plug-in variance estimation was already disclosed in v1, and v2 supplies no new estimator recipe, code access or computing-resource details.

R1.justification: V2 adds Agrawal and Goyal (2013), Snoek et al. (2012), Zhu and Rigotti (2021), and Zhu and Kveton (2022b). It connects the likelihood construction to prior work and adds a short comparison with Bayesian optimization. The principal positioning as an extension of random-effect bandits to BAI remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes local prose corrections, expands explanations and reorganizes Section 5.1, moving the small-variance versus small-gap discussion into Section 3. Appendices A–G become A.1–A.7, and author contributions receive a separate heading. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 replaces misleading K = 20, 40 and 80 headings with F1–F3 and labels the remaining panels F4–F6. The scaling figure gains TTTS curves and a legend entry. Appendix figures are renumbered S.1/S.2 to 3/4; the overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: The corrected gap definition and theoretical constants, accurate Figure 2 labels and fuller acknowledgment of TTTS exceptions improve precision and interpretation. Additional TTTS scaling results modestly strengthen the empirical comparison. The gains are limited: the core method and main results remain unchanged, and Section 5.2 still omits the factors of two added to the appendix tail bounds.
